reasons: Section 11.1 provides zero transition assistance and mandates immediate permanent deletion with no export/migration support, which fails the fallback (90 days assistance) and sits in walk-away territory, so the deviation classification is correct even though §§ 11.2–11.3 already satisfy the data-return and certified-deletion elements.

The redline is directionally right and actionable: it replaces only the offending sentence with the preferred six-month, then-current-rates transition assistance plus export/migration support, and subordinates deletion to §§ 11.2–11.3, avoiding duplication of the already-compliant return/deletion mechanics.

The failed 'minimal edit' check is acceptable here — the original sentence was entirely walk-away language, so a full replacement is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position; no salvageable customer-favourable text was removed.
Comment is concise, in first person plural, accurately describes the change, cites the internal contradiction with §§ 11.2–11.3, and offers the 90-day fallback as required by the rule.
